channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Trump says record Navy deployment in Iran operations 'not nearly long enough'
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday dismissed concerns about the toll on sailors aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, who have endured a record deployment of almost nine months, saying that the deployment had been “not nearly long enough”. The Lincoln has been supporting the US war against Iran, and reports have emerged of sailors struggling with mental health issues.
item.source: © Jason Waite, US Navy via AFP file photo
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Teenage British cyclist Finlay ⁠Tarling dies in Tour of Portugal accident
item.description: 19-year-old British cyclist Finlay ⁠Tarling died ​following a "serious accident" during the eighth stage ​of the Tour of Portugal race, tour organisers and his team said on Friday.
item.source: © Alberto Astudillo, ZUMA Press Wire via Reuters

item.title: Kenya: Mysterious illness kills more than a dozen elephants
item.description: In Kenya, since the end of June, at least 19 elephants, mostly females or young animals, have died after displaying the same symptoms, notably partial paralysis preventing them from standing.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Race to free trapped quake survivor offers hope in Colombia
item.description: Rescue workers rushed to free a survivor Friday in Colombia amid the rubble left by a powerful earthquake nearly four days earlier that killed at least 285 people and injured 4,000. Some 400 people were still missing and tens of thousands of homes were ​damaged, leaving many Colombians sleeping in shelters or outside.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: ‘We never leave’: Palestinians besieged in West Bank fear Israeli settlers will seize their homes
item.description: For nearly a week, Israeli settlers have been surrounding homes in the West bank village of Qusra in a coordinated offensive to force Palestinian residents from their homes in order to seize new land.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Europe: Raging wildfires scorch large swaths of the continent
item.description: Firefighters across Europe battled multiple fires August 14 as a new wave of record-breaking heat baked a swath of the continent. The historic temperatures are linked to human-caused climate change, and are hitting countries better suited for long cold seasons and ill-equipped for such extreme heat, with limited air conditioning.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France wildfire forces 520 to evacuate
item.description: Around 520 residents in France’s southwestern Landes region have been evacuated as a raging wildfire has burned through more than 1,000 hectares since Thursday. Significant reinforcements have been mobilised, while authorities warn that the fire’s trajectory remains unpredictable. Simon Moritz has the story.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France blocks under 15 social media ban
item.description: France’s Constitutional Council has blocked a bill that would have banned social media access for under-15s, ruling that it infringed on freedom of expression. It’s a setback for President Emmanuel Macron, who has championed the legislation and has now asked his prime minister to rewrite the bill. The Élysée says Macron remains determined to have the reform in place before next year’s presidential election. France 24 International Affairs editor tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: West Bank: Washington condemns siege of Palestinian homes
item.description: Settlers have been besieging homes in Qusra ​for almost a week, intensifying ‌pressure on Palestinians.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Birthrate drop in North Africa
item.description: The Maghreb region is experiencing a dramatic decline in birth rates, with most women now having fewer than three children, compared with seven or eight on average in the 1970s. Ellen Gainsford looks at what is driving this major demographic shift.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: World Bank to fund 645-metre bridge linking Bangui and Zongo
item.description: The Central African Republic and the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to build a new bridge linking their two major cities, Bangui and Zongo. The 60-million-dollar project will see the construction of a 645-metre bridge across the Congo River, aimed at strengthening trade and transport links between the two countries.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Mount Etna continues to erupt in Italy
item.description: Flights at Catania airport in Sicily remain suspended because of ongoing volcanic activity from Mount Etna. But for those already on the island, the spectacular lava flows have become a major attraction, drawing crowds of tourists to safe viewing points. Companies organising guided nighttime hikes say they have been flooded with calls from visitors hoping to see the eruption up close. Etna is Europe’s largest active volcano, and the latest activity has been unusual for its persistence and sustained ash emissions. Emily Boyle reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Chadian President Déby pardons jailed main rival and 8 opposition leaders
item.description: Chad’s President Mahamat Idriss Déby on Friday pardoned the jailed ex-prime minister and leader of Chad’s main opposition party Succès Masra, along with eight other party leaders. Masra had been serving a 20-year sentence, convicted of hate speech, xenophobia and inciting a massacre, in what Human Rights Watch called a politically motivated trial.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: France's constitutional authority strikes down social media ban for under-15s
item.description: France's constitutional council struck down a proposed ban on social media for children under 15 on Friday, citing freedom of expression. President Emmanuel Macron tasked Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu with re-working ​the draft legislation to take the Constitutional Council's concerns into account, the Elysée said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Mount Etna's ongoing volcanic activity disrupts summer travel
item.description: Ash spewing from Sicily's Mount Etna has closed the Italian island’s largest airport for the fifth consecutive day, stranding hundreds of summer holiday travellers during the busiest travel week of the year. Catania’s airport will remain closed until early August 15. While Etna, Europe's largest active volcano, often disrupts airport operations, this marks the longest emergency since 2002.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Zambia suspends vote count nationwide amid reports of violence, ballot theft
item.description: Zambia's electoral commission on Friday suspended vote counting from Thursday's presidential and parliamentary elections for at least 24 hours due to “violence targeted at poll staff” and reported instances of theft of marked ballot papers. Former minister Brian Mundubile, the main challenger to President Hakainde Hichilema, claimed a first-round victory and said his camp viewed "the continued delay ... with grave concern".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Japan: Record rains kill eight, strand thousands at Narita airport
item.description: Record rainfall has caused deadly flooding in Japan, leaving thousands stranded at Narita Airport during the Obon holiday period.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ferry sinking kills 46 in rural Zimbabwe
item.description: In Zimbabwe, hundreds of people have attended a memorial service following a ferry disaster on Lake Kariba that claimed at least 46 lives. The boat was a vital link for villagers and fish traders around the vast lake, but was reportedly overloaded when it ran into trouble on Tuesday. Laurent Berstecher has the details.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Europe swelters under fifth heatwave of summer
item.description: A large part of Europe is in the grip of its fifth heatwave of the summer, with temperatures in parts of France soaring to 40 degrees Celsius. And the extreme weather is also taking a toll on the world’s oceans: last month, average global sea temperatures reached a record high of 21 degrees Celsius. Chair of the National Heat Risk Commission at Grantham Research Institute, at LSE, Emma Howard Boyd, shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: West Bank: Palestinians families trapped in home
item.description: Israeli settlers are carrying out a campaign of violence and intimidation against the Palestinian village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank, where families have had their electricity and water supplies cut off, in what residents say is an attempt to force them from their homes. France 24 Senior Reporter Catherine Norris Trent recalls reporting from Qusra in 2023, when villagers told her that Israeli settlers were attacking them, preventing them from accessing their land and threatening them with violence if they tried to harvest their olives. The attacks came amid a sharp increase in settler violence in the West Bank following the October 7 Hamas attack, although villagers said such violence had been going on for years and was already making their lives increasingly difficult by 2023.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: West Bank: Palestinians families trapped in homes
item.description:
Israeli settlers are conducting a campaign of violence and intimidation against the Palestinian village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank. Families have had their electricity and water supplies cut off, in what residents say is an attempt to force them from their homes.
According to France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky, Israel’s Defence Minister is using settler violence for political propaganda, as the army could remove violent settlers but is not ordered to do so due to far-right political pressure. The situation is expected to remain unchanged, with the army standing by as armed settlers intimidate Palestinians.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukraine war: Grain attacks raise food price fears
item.description: Ukraine and Russia have been trading attacks on each other’s grain warehouses, raising concerns that the damage to food supplies could push global food prices higher. France 24 International affairs editor Philippe Turle shares more insights on the subject.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
